text.p: The following are some of the leading stories in Finnish papers this morning.
- Conservative party MPs furious with Social Democrats, say they went back on compromise decision on shop opening hours and short-term labour contracts.
- Men in Finland's Swedish-speaking communities live longer than those in other parts of the country, have fewer occupational accidents. @
- UN human rights committee supports National Board of Forestry's view that tree cutting in the Muotkatunturi area in far north does not violate rights of reindeer herders.
- Nokia among bidders to supply set-top decoders to News Corporation's BSkyB, which plans to launch 200-channel digital television service in Britain next year.
- European Commission denies tax-free status to xylitol birch-based sweetener, made by foods group Cultor and used by sweets maker Huhtamaki. @
- Chemicals group Kemira's Tikkurila unit building paint factory in Pennsylvania with McWhorter Technologies Inc.
- State tax revenues to fall below budget this year, says Finance Ministry's Raimo Sailas.
- Investment Bank Morgan Stanley sees good prospects for Finnish economic growth up to end of the decade, but says markets' confidence in Finnish EMU membership has weakened. @
- Unlike other Nordic countries, Finland did not want last week's meeting of the World Trade Organisation in Singapore to deal with question of basic workers' rights.
- Parliament gave strong backing to continued participation of Finnish peacekeepers in Bosnia mission. MPs praised the way mission has been run.

- Central Union of Agricultural Producers and Forest Owners, MTK, welcomes EU Commission decision to allow new Finnish system of direct timber sales negotiations between forestry companies and forest owners for five years. @

- Nokia expects its Communicator, combining mobile phone, fax and Internet capabilities, to become a mass demand product, like today's conventional mobile phones, but says the new device will not have a big impact on earnings this year.
